# Generalised additive mixed model

This script gives the following results for the generalised additive mixed model, separately for the aligned Big Five scores and the BFI-S items: the cross-validated performance, the training-set and hold-out performance, and the smooth-term summaries. The training-set models are saved for the smooth-figure scripts. The printed tables are saved so those results can be read again without refitting.

## Modelling sample

The cleaning below is the same code as in Han and gives the same modelling sample as in the other analysis scripts.

```{r}
# The packages for the data, the model, and the performance measures are loaded.
library(tidyverse)
library(mgcv)
library(rsample)
library(yardstick)

# The aligned data are loaded.
load("covid_aligned_BFF.RData")

# Country, gender, and education are stored as factors.
data_NEU.aligned$Country<-as.factor(data_NEU.aligned$Country)
data_NEU.aligned$Dem_gender<-as.factor(data_NEU.aligned$Dem_gender)
data_NEU.aligned$Dem_edu<-as.factor(data_NEU.aligned$Dem_edu)

# Rows with missing age, gender, or education are removed.
data<-data_NEU.aligned[
  !is.na(data_NEU.aligned$Dem_age)&
  !is.na(data_NEU.aligned$Dem_edu)&
  !is.na(data_NEU.aligned$Dem_gender),]

# Country is recoded to numbers and stored as a factor. The models use this version.
data$country<-as.numeric(data$Country)
data$country<-as.factor(data$country)
```

## Training set

The split below is the same participant-level split as in the other analyses. Cross-validation is done inside the training set. The hold-out set is used only for the final performance (Methods section).

```{r}
set.seed(17)

# The participants are divided into a training set with 80% and a hold-out set with 20%.
data_split <- group_initial_split(data, group = ID, prop = 0.8)
train_set <- training(data_split)
holdout_set <- testing(data_split)

# The training set is divided into five folds for cross-validation.
cv_folds <- group_vfold_cv(train_set, group = ID, v = 5)

# The sample sizes of the training set and the hold-out set are printed.
nrow(train_set)
nrow(holdout_set)
```

## Models

Both models contain a smooth for each personality predictor and for age. Gender and education are categorical predictors, and country is a random intercept. The two models differ only in the personality predictors. The basis dimension is \(k = 10\) for the aligned scores and \(k = 5\) for the items, and age uses the same basis dimension (Methods section).

```{r}
# The personality predictors of the two models are the five aligned scores and the 15 items.
trait_predictors <- c("NEU", "EXT", "OPE", "AGR", "CON")
item_predictors <- paste0("BFF_15_", 1:15)

# The aligned-score model has a random intercept for country and smooths with k = 10 for the five scores and age.
# Gender and education are categorical predictors. Columns ending in _z are standardised.
trait_formula <- Compliance_2 ~ s(country, bs = "re") +
  s(NEU_z, bs = "tp", k = 10) + s(EXT_z, bs = "tp", k = 10) +
  s(OPE_z, bs = "tp", k = 10) + s(AGR_z, bs = "tp", k = 10) +
  s(CON_z, bs = "tp", k = 10) + s(Dem_age_z, bs = "tp", k = 10) +
  Dem_gender + Dem_edu

# The item model has the same structure, with smooths with k = 5 for the 15 items and age.
item_formula <- Compliance_2 ~ s(country, bs = "re") +
  s(BFF_15_1_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) + s(BFF_15_2_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) +
  s(BFF_15_3_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) + s(BFF_15_4_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) +
  s(BFF_15_5_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) + s(BFF_15_6_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) +
  s(BFF_15_7_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) + s(BFF_15_8_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) +
  s(BFF_15_9_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) + s(BFF_15_10_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) +
  s(BFF_15_11_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) + s(BFF_15_12_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) +
  s(BFF_15_13_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) + s(BFF_15_14_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) +
  s(BFF_15_15_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) + s(Dem_age_z, bs = "tp", k = 5) +
  Dem_gender + Dem_edu

# This function fits a GAMM by REML. Each smooth can be shrunk to zero if it does not improve the fit.
fit_gamm <- function(formula, data) {
  gam(formula, family = gaussian(), method = "REML", select = TRUE, data = data)
}
```

## Performance

The same three functions are used for both predictor representations. `evaluate()` fits one model and calculates its performance. `cross_validate()` repeats this in the five training-set folds. `final_performance()` fits the model once to the complete training set and scores it on the hold-out set. The smooth summaries use this training-set fit. \(R^2\) is calculated with `rsq_trad`. In the printed tables, Assessment is the left-out fold during cross-validation and the hold-out set in the final performance.

```{r}
# RMSE, MAE, and R2 are the performance measures. rmse and mae are taken from yardstick.
performance_metrics <- metric_set(yardstick::rmse, yardstick::mae, rsq_trad)

# This function standardises the given predictors with the mean and standard deviation of the reference data.
# The standardised values are stored in new columns ending in _z.
standardise <- function(data, reference_data, predictors) {
  centre <- map_dbl(reference_data[predictors], mean)
  spread <- map_dbl(reference_data[predictors], sd)
  data[paste0(predictors, "_z")] <- scale(data[predictors], center = centre, scale = spread)
  data
}

# This function fits one model and calculates its performance in the fitting data and in new data.
# The new data are the left-out fold during cross-validation and the hold-out set in the final performance.
evaluate <- function(formula, predictors, fit_data, new_data) {
  # Age and the personality predictors are standardised in both data sets with the mean and standard deviation of the fitting data.
  numeric_predictors <- c(predictors, "Dem_age")
  fit_data <- standardise(fit_data, fit_data, numeric_predictors)
  new_data <- standardise(new_data, fit_data, numeric_predictors)

  # The GAMM is fitted, and general compliance is predicted in both data sets.
  model <- fit_gamm(formula, fit_data)
  fit_data$.pred <- predict(model, newdata = fit_data)
  new_data$.pred <- predict(model, newdata = new_data)

  # RMSE, MAE, and R2 are calculated in both data sets, labelled Training and Assessment.
  metrics <- bind_rows(
    Training = performance_metrics(fit_data, Compliance_2, .pred),
    Assessment = performance_metrics(new_data, Compliance_2, .pred),
    .id = "set"
  )

  # The performance and the fitted model are returned.
  list(metrics = metrics, model = model)
}

# This function runs the five-fold cross-validation and summarises the performance.
cross_validate <- function(formula, predictors) {
  # In each fold, the model is fitted to the other four folds and scored on the left-out fold. Only the performance is kept.
  folds <- map_dfr(
    cv_folds$splits,
    function(split) {
      evaluate(formula, predictors, analysis(split), assessment(split))$metrics
    },
    .id = "fold"
  )

  # The mean and standard deviation across the five folds are calculated and rounded to three decimals.
  cv_summary <- folds %>%
    group_by(set, .metric) %>%
    summarise(mean = round(mean(.estimate), 3), sd = round(sd(.estimate), 3), .groups = "drop")

  # In each fold, the validation R2 is subtracted from the training R2.
  # The mean and standard deviation of this difference are then calculated.
  delta_r2 <- folds %>%
    filter(.metric == "rsq_trad") %>%
    pivot_wider(id_cols = fold, names_from = set, values_from = .estimate) %>%
    summarise(mean = round(mean(Training - Assessment), 3), sd = round(sd(Training - Assessment), 3))

  # The performance summary and the R2 difference are returned.
  list(summary = cv_summary, delta_r2 = delta_r2)
}

# This function fits the model once to the complete training set and scores it on the hold-out set.
final_performance <- function(formula, predictors) {
  fitted <- evaluate(formula, predictors, train_set, holdout_set)
  results <- fitted$metrics

  # The unrounded training R2 and hold-out R2 are extracted.
  training_r2 <- results %>%
    filter(set == "Training", .metric == "rsq_trad") %>%
    pull(.estimate)
  holdout_r2 <- results %>%
    filter(set == "Assessment", .metric == "rsq_trad") %>%
    pull(.estimate)

  # The rounded performance, the R2 difference, and the training-set model are returned.
  # The R2 difference is calculated from the unrounded values and then rounded.
  list(
    metrics = mutate(results, .estimate = round(.estimate, 3)),
    delta_r2 = round(training_r2 - holdout_r2, 3),
    model = fitted$model
  )
}
```

### Aligned Big Five scores

The code below first calculates the cross-validated performance and then the training-set and hold-out performance for the aligned Big Five scores (Supplementary Table S4, then Table 1 and Supplementary Table S3).

```{r}
# The cross-validated performance is calculated and printed (Supplementary Table S4).
trait_cv <- cross_validate(trait_formula, trait_predictors)
trait_cv

# The training-set and hold-out performance and the R2 difference are calculated and printed (Table 1; Supplementary Table S3).
# The training-set model is saved for Figure 6.
trait_final <- final_performance(trait_formula, trait_predictors)
trait_final$metrics
trait_final$delta_r2
saveRDS(trait_final$model, "gamm_trait_model.rds")
```

### BFI-S items

The code below first calculates the cross-validated performance and then the training-set and hold-out performance for the BFI-S items (Supplementary Table S4, then Table 1 and Supplementary Table S3).

```{r}
# The cross-validated performance is calculated and printed (Supplementary Table S4).
item_cv <- cross_validate(item_formula, item_predictors)
item_cv

# The training-set and hold-out performance and the R2 difference are calculated and printed (Table 1; Supplementary Table S3).
# The training-set model is saved for Supplementary Figure S2.
item_final <- final_performance(item_formula, item_predictors)
item_final$metrics
item_final$delta_r2
saveRDS(item_final$model, "gamm_item_model.rds")
```

## Smooth terms

The summaries below use the training-set models already fitted for the hold-out performance. EDF describes the curvature of a smooth: values near 1 are approximately linear. \(\Delta\mathrm{AIC}\) is the AIC of the model with that predictor entered as a straight line minus the AIC of the model with that predictor entered as a smooth. Positive values favour the smooth (Supplementary Tables S6 and S7).

```{r}
# This function builds the comparison formula.
# One personality predictor is entered as a straight line, and all other terms stay as in the full model.
linear_formula <- function(predictors, linear_predictor, k) {
  # The selected predictor is linear, and the other personality predictors remain smooths.
  personality_terms <- if_else(
    predictors == linear_predictor,
    paste0(predictors, "_z"),
    paste0("s(", predictors, "_z, bs = 'tp', k = ", k, ")")
  )
  # Country, age, gender, and education are added as in the full model.
  reformulate(
    c(
      "s(country, bs = 're')",
      personality_terms,
      paste0("s(Dem_age_z, bs = 'tp', k = ", k, ")"),
      "Dem_gender",
      "Dem_edu"
    ),
    response = "Compliance_2"
  )
}

# This function returns one row per personality predictor with EDF, F, p, and delta AIC.
smooth_comparison <- function(model, predictors, k) {
  # EDF, F, and p are taken from the model summary, and the AIC of the full model is stored.
  smooth_names <- paste0("s(", predictors, "_z)")
  smooth_statistics <- summary(model)$s.table[smooth_names, c("edf", "F", "p-value")]
  full_smooth_aic <- AIC(model)

  # For each predictor, the model is refitted with only that predictor entered as a straight line.
  # Delta AIC is the AIC of that model minus the AIC of the full model. The refit uses the training data stored in the model.
  delta_aic <- map_dbl(predictors, function(predictor) {
    comparison_formula <- linear_formula(predictors, predictor, k)
    linear_comparison_model <- fit_gamm(
      comparison_formula,
      data = model$model
    )
    AIC(linear_comparison_model) - full_smooth_aic
  })

  # The results are rounded for the table. p-values below .001 are written as <.001.
  tibble(
    predictor = predictors,
    edf = round(smooth_statistics[, "edf"], 2),
    F = round(smooth_statistics[, "F"], 2),
    p = if_else(
      smooth_statistics[, "p-value"] < 0.001,
      "<.001",
      format(round(smooth_statistics[, "p-value"], 3), nsmall = 3)
    ),
    delta_aic = round(delta_aic, 1)
  )
}
```

### Aligned Big Five scores

The code below compares each aligned-score smooth with a linear term and prints the smooth-term summary (Supplementary Table S6).

```{r}
# The aligned-score smooths are summarised and printed in the order conscientiousness, agreeableness, openness, extraversion, and neuroticism.
trait_smooths <- smooth_comparison(
  trait_final$model,
  trait_predictors,
  k = 10
) %>%
  arrange(factor(predictor, levels = c("CON", "AGR", "OPE", "EXT", "NEU")))
trait_smooths
```

### BFI-S items

The code below compares each item smooth with a linear term and prints the smooth-term summary (Supplementary Table S7).

```{r}
# The item smooths are summarised and printed in item order.
item_smooths <- smooth_comparison(
  item_final$model,
  item_predictors,
  k = 5
)
item_smooths

# The performance tables and smooth summaries are saved in one file, so they can be read without refitting.
saveRDS(
  list(
    trait_cv = trait_cv,
    trait_final = list(metrics = trait_final$metrics, delta_r2 = trait_final$delta_r2),
    item_cv = item_cv,
    item_final = list(metrics = item_final$metrics, delta_r2 = item_final$delta_r2),
    trait_smooths = trait_smooths,
    item_smooths = item_smooths
  ),
  "gamm_results.rds"
)
```
